source: workflow wf_b6831f59-4aa (probe-phase-c-ir): lens observations + independent skeptic verdicts, verbatim.

observations.statement: Codex reasoning_output_tokens values pile onto a lattice at 516 + 518k (516, 1034, 1552, 2070, 2588, 3106, 4142). The neighbouring values are empty, and almost all lattice hits come from gpt-5.4.
observations.numbers: 516: 111 usage rows in 27 sessions; counts at the +-4 neighbours are [1,4,5,3 | 0,1,0,0]. 1034: 16 rows, neighbours [2,2,1,1 | 0,0,0,0]. On-lattice share 140/6910 = 0.020 [0.016, 0.028] over 68 sessions. By model, on-lattice rows / all rows: gpt-5.4 136/5809, gpt-5.4-mini 3/101, gpt-5.3-codex 1/1000. Profile spike at 516: count 138, 85.8x its local density.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Unknown. The counter is provider-written. Neighbours are empty on the high side only, which looks like a counter that snaps or saturates in chunks of about 518 tokens. UNVERIFIED.

observations.statement: In AI Village computer use, 46% of all 78k sessions have exactly 41 turns (40 model turns plus 1 synthetic bootstrap turn). The spike appears in every stratum except the Agent-SDK one.
observations.numbers: 35684/78114 = 0.457 [0.453, 0.460]. By stratum, from 0.226 (openai-chat) to 0.677 [0.663, 0.690] (haiku). anthropic-claude-code: 1/862. Exactly 40 model turns: 31473 sessions. Neighbouring lengths: 40 turns 1514, 42 turns 4300.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Inferred harness turn cap of 40 model turns per session. Session ends are censored, not task completions. No harness config is in the data.

observations.statement: Gemini prompt-side image token counts are exact multiples of a per-image cost (flash: 1064; pro: 258 or 1064). Cached image token counts are not.
observations.numbers: flash: 3219/3219 divisible by 1064 (90 sessions). pro: 10499/10569 = 0.993 [0.984, 1.0] divisible by 258 or 1064. Spike mass 0.993 (flash) and 0.989 (pro). Cached IMAGE on the lattice: 11/3022 and 40/9318; their parity is 0.495 and 0.490.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Fixed token cost per image (two sizes on pro). Inferred from the lattice: server-side usage encodes the image count in context.

observations.statement: In 73 swechat Claude Code sessions, Edit and Write calls show a 5.0-5.2 s latency plateau. The time is spent inside the tool before the PostToolUse hook; hooks do not explain it.
observations.numbers: Calls in [4900, 5200) ms: Edit 644/28793 = 0.022 [0.011, 0.038] in 73 sessions; Write 28/4478 = 0.006; Read 7/55258. In the plateau, PostToolUse progress comes a median 5020 ms after the call and +1 ms after the result stamp. PreToolUse progress appears on 4/644 plateau calls vs 5588/26323 Edits under 1 s. Exact-value spikes at 5014-5021 ms.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Unknown. Some fixed ~5 s wait in the file-mutation path in some environments (an editor/diagnostics timeout is a guess). UNVERIFIED.

observations.statement: Claude Code truncates failed-command shell output near 10,040 chars and successful output at 30,000 chars. OpenCode's cap is near 51,551.
observations.numbers: swechat CC results with an 'Exit code' prefix: 205/3237 (122 sessions) within 1% of the max 10050; values 10039 x100 and 10040 x79. Successful output: max 29766, no pile. cc_local successful output: max 30000 (3 at the max). aiv_cc failed output: max 10040. OpenCode shell: 91/1859 (85 sessions) within 1% of 51551.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Harness truncation limits that differ by exit status. The cap values are inferred from where values pile up.

observations.statement: AI Village updated_at is not a second clock: it equals created_at to within microseconds.
observations.numbers: 59834/59956 rows within 0.01 ms (1979 sessions); median 0.002 ms. Only 17 rows exceed 1 s: 0.00028 [0.00015, 0.00043]. 0 negative. 0 of the 17 are redacted.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Both fields are set at row insert. The raw census's candidate second clock carries no independent timing.

observations.statement: Uncached input tokens (usage_in) collapse onto one or two constants per harness.
observations.numbers: swechat CC: 1 in 0.697 of 158061, Hill alpha 0.445 [0.396, 0.507]. cc_local: 2 in 0.922. aiv_cc: only 8 (0.858) and 10 (0.142), so step = 2. aiv_cu Agent-SDK: 8/10 in 0.845/0.155. aiv_cu direct API: 10 in 0.259 (opus), 0.249 (sonnet), 0.436 (haiku).
observations.mechanical_explanation: Prompt caching leaves only a fixed framing suffix uncached, and the constant is set by harness version. Inferred.

observations.statement: File order is not time order in honest logs.
observations.numbers: swechat CC consecutive gaps negative 0.047 [0.044, 0.050] (40243/855208). hook_progress->result gaps: 0.529 [0.504, 0.554] negative, 0.428 zero. OpenCode result->call: 0.300 [0.251, 0.367] negative. 57 CC results precede their call in seq.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Measured for CC: the result carries the tool-completion stamp, while the PostToolUse hook progress is stamped +1 ms later but written earlier in the file. OpenCode: parallel tool parts.

observations.statement: Claude Code bash_progress events tick at 1 Hz with 0-4 ms jitter.
observations.numbers: 0.877 [0.848, 0.902] of 115088 consecutive bash_progress gaps (668 sessions) fall on 1000-1004+ ms. Shares: 1001 ms 0.319, 1000 0.176, 1002 0.169. p50 1001 ms, p99 1219 ms.
observations.mechanical_explanation: 1 s progress timer. Inferred.

observations.statement: Call->result latency has tail index ~1 (infinite variance), and timeouts explain little of the extreme tail.
observations.numbers: Hill alpha: swechat CC 1.028 [0.975, 1.091], cc_local 1.007 [0.757, 1.221], OpenCode 0.580 [0.438, 2.626]. swechat CC p99/p50 = 2513 [2054, 3162]. Calls that reached their timeout argument: 535/14166 = 0.038 [0.031, 0.045]. Top-1% CC shell latencies at a timeout: 56/611; cc_local 27/269.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Timeouts are measured. The rest is unmeasured (long or background commands, human approval waits not in IR).

observations.statement: Logged output_tokens are streaming snapshots, with a large mode at exactly 1.
observations.numbers: usage_out == 1: swechat CC 0.169; aiv_cc 0.618; aiv_cu Agent-SDK 0.680. swechat CC has 3 stable modes (1, 27, 154). Spikes at 8000 (13 values in 9 sessions) and 8192 (12 values in 2 sessions).
observations.mechanical_explanation: Per-block rows written mid-stream. The 8000/8192 values are possibly max-token caps; stop_reason is not in the IR.

observations.statement: Polling produces identical outputs thousands of times.
observations.numbers: aiv_cc get_events empty-feed payloads: 3764 chars x1568 (3 sessions) and 3679 x1287 (3 sessions, top session 0.998); spike mass 0.558 [0.497, 0.602]. Codex yield_time_ms is 1000 in 0.894 of calls; latency within [yield, yield+300 ms) for 0.329 [0.061, 0.390] of 3382 calls; median latency - yield = -110 ms.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Agent polling loops plus the unified-exec yield window. Measured.

observations.statement: Harness templates dominate several tools' output-length distributions.
observations.numbers: CC TaskUpdate 22 chars: 0.738. Grep 'No matches found': 0.160. Glob 'No files found': 0.217. '(Bash completed with no output)': 2343. cc_local total_tokens_reminder at 86/49 chars: 13611+12054 of 36306 system events. aiv_cu 'Message successfully sent back to chat': 2615. Who&When HC 'Next speaker WebSurfer': 331/934.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Fixed harness strings. Measured from prefixes; enum labels only for cc_local.

observations.statement: aiv_cc's stderr and Read channels hold mostly harness notices.
observations.numbers: stderr: 0.470 [0.221, 0.694] of 4919 values are the 93-char 'Shell cwd was reset to /home/<user>...' notice (19 sessions); the rest are empty. Read results: 2530/2914 = 0.868 are the string '[image]'.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Harness cwd-reset notice; images stripped from the export.

observations.statement: Numbers the agent chooses are round and come from a small vocabulary. Harness timers and counters show no round-number excess unless they echo an agent's choice or hit a cap or timer.
observations.numbers: CC shell timeout: 0.978 of 14195 values on 16 spike values; 120000 ms = 0.272; 736/736 values >= 600 s are whole minutes. head/tail -n: 875/878 of values >= 100 are multiples of 10. sleep: 709/709 whole seconds. Only 31 round-number flags among 690 profiles in total.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Model-chosen parameters (expected). 120000 is the CC default written out explicitly.

observations.statement: No timestamp quantization in any corpus or stratum.
observations.numbers: Share of stamps with ms field 000 is about 0.001 everywhere (swechat CC 0.00096 [0.00087, 0.00104], n 856886); ms % 10 == 0 about 0.1.
observations.mechanical_explanation: All sources write full ms or us stamps (aiv strips trailing zeros).

observations.statement: Most quantities are featureless, including thinking/reasoning lengths and session-level counts.
observations.numbers: 293/690 profiled quantities have one mode, no spike, no round flag and no negative values. Thinking/reasoning profiles: 32/38 featureless, 3 with spikes, 3 multimodal. Session level: 93/192 featureless. aiv_cu turn gaps are unimodal in 9/10 strata.
observations.mechanical_explanation: n/a

observations.statement: The IR files harness interrupt markers under kind 'user'.
observations.mechanical_explanation: '[Request interrupted by user]' and '[... for tool use]' are harness text that cc_jsonl classifies as user. This inflates n_user and user_text_chars.

observations.statement: The Gemini HTTP Date header always precedes the row insert time.
observations.numbers: Negative in 3264/3264 rows (flash) and 9028/9028 (pro). Medians -4.4 s / -4.6 s; the closest values are -78 ms and -112 ms.
observations.mechanical_explanation: The response header is stamped before the action executes and the row is inserted.

observations.statement: Constants that fingerprint a scaffold version or an automation recur across sessions.
observations.numbers: OpenCode first-request usage_in 7174 occurs once in each of 52 sessions. OpenCode 4657-char 'You are a code reviewer' prompt opens 106/214 sessions. cc_local 2074-char user text in 150/186 sessions. Codex model_context_window takes only 258400 (0.775) or 950000 (0.225).
observations.mechanical_explanation: Fixed system/automation prompts and per-model config constants.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Provider usage-lattice plausibility check
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Check reported prompt image tokens: they must be a sum of per-image costs (Gemini 1064/258). Check cache_read: it must be a multiple of the provider block (Codex 128). Honest on-lattice rate: 10499/10569 (pro), 3219/3219 (flash), Codex cache 1.0.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Off-lattice honest rows (70/10569 on pro). Model or version changes in per-image cost. Cached image tokens are never on the lattice, so only prompt-side counts can be checked.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED; possibly undescribed for agent-log fabrication detection. Not checked against the literature.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Harness-conformance fingerprint (cadence, templates, caps, uncached-input constant)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Check four things: bash_progress gaps sit at 1000-1004 ms (0.877 of honest gaps); exact template strings and lengths; tool output never exceeds the harness cap (CC 30000 / ~10050 on failure; OpenCode 51551); usage_in equals the harness constant (1, 2, or 8/10).
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Scheduling jitter (only 0.877 of ticks on cadence). Template and cap changes across versions. Failure max 10050 vs a pile at 10039/10040. This tests log provenance, not the truth of tool results.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED; resembles generic log-format validation.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Strict server-clock ordering (Gemini HTTP Date < row insert)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Test date header < created_at on every Gemini row. It holds in 12292/12292 rows, with a minimum margin of 78 ms.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Clock skew between the server and the DB host. The header has 1 s resolution, so it catches only gross time edits.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED; standard timestamp-consistency auditing.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Reasoning-token lattice as a model fingerprint (session/corpus level)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: A log claiming gpt-5.4 should show about 0.020 [0.016, 0.028] of token_count rows at 516 + 518k, with empty neighbours.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Unknown mechanism, so it may change with provider updates. The share is low, so the test has no per-row power.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED; the lattice itself may be undocumented.

could_not_measure: Cause of the Edit/Write 5.0-5.2 s plateau: the IR has no environment, IDE or hook-config fields (hooks are excluded: PreToolUse appears on 4/644 plateau calls).
Cause of the Codex reasoning_output_tokens 516 + 518k lattice: only token_count events, no provider documentation.
Whether 41 turns is a configured AI Village cap: no harness config in the data.
What makes up the latency tail beyond timeouts: human permission waits and backgrounded commands are not in the IR.
Whether the 8000/8192 output-token spikes are max-token stops: stop_reason is not in the IR.
Who&When shapes: no timestamps, and session-level quantities (including mistake_step) fall below min_n with 78/33 sessions.
Cursor: no timestamps and no results; 8 Phase B sessions.
cc_local content-level attribution: private corpus, so only enum labels and lengths.
Sub-second ordering against the Gemini HTTP Date: the header has 1 s resolution.

checks.my_numbers: Codex token_count rows that carry usage: 6910 rows in 68 sessions. Value 516: 111 rows in 27 sessions, ±4 neighbours [1,4,5,3 | 0,1,0,0]. Value 1034: 16 rows in 10 sessions, neighbours [2,2,1,1 | 0,0,0,0]. On-lattice: 140/6910 = 0.020 [0.016, 0.028]. Counting repeated rows (7154): 516 x138, 173 on-lattice. Per-row on-lattice rate by model: gpt-5.4 136/5809 = 0.023; gpt-5.4-mini 3/101 = 0.030; gpt-5.3-codex 1/1000 = 0.001. Density: 1.79 rows per token value in [400,516), then 0.72 in [517,633).
checks.problem: The numbers reproduce exactly. 'Almost all hits come from gpt-5.4' is mostly a base-rate effect: gpt-5.4 makes up 84% of rows, and gpt-5.4-mini hits the lattice at the same or a higher rate (0.030). The real contrast is the gpt-5.4 family against gpt-5.3-codex. The high-side neighbours are not fully empty (+2 at 516 has 1). Density drops by more than half just above 516, which fits a pile-up but does not identify a mechanism. Keep the cause as unknown.

checks.my_numbers: 35684/78114 = 0.457 [0.453, 0.460]. Session counts: 40 turns 1514, 42 turns 4300, more than 41 turns 7024, exactly 40 model turns 31473. Agent-SDK stratum 1/862; haiku 0.677 [0.663, 0.690]; openai-chat 0.226. Synthetic turns among the 41-turn sessions: 1 in 31360, 0 in 4318. Share of 41-turn sessions by month of first turn: 0.23-0.39 before 2026-04, 0.75 in 2026-04, 0.46-0.60 after. Max turns: 326 (gemini-pro), 208 (compat-chat).

The cap is soft: 9% of sessions exceed 41 turns, up to 326. The spike's share changes over time. Nothing in the data shows whether sessions were 'censored, not task completions'.

checks.my_numbers: flash: 3219/3219 divisible by 1064 (90 sessions). pro: 10499/10569 = 0.993 [0.984, 1.0]. The 70 off-lattice pro rows are all multiples of 2160 (3 sessions, gemini-3-pro-preview), so 10569/10569 sit on {258, 1064, 2160}. By model: gemini-2.5-pro* → 258 only (6383 rows); gemini-3/3.1-pro-preview → 1064 (4116 rows) or 2160 (70 rows). No session mixes lattices (0/309). Cached IMAGE on the lattice: 11/3022 and 40/9318; parity 0.495 and 0.490. Cached is always below the prompt IMAGE count (1.0).
checks.problem: The mechanical explanation is wrong in detail. Pro does not have 'two image sizes': the lattice constant is set by model generation (2.5 → 258, 3.x → 1064), and there is a third constant, 2160, in 3 sessions. The 0.7% residual is fully explained by that third lattice.

checks.my_numbers: Calls in [4900, 5200) ms: Edit 644/28793 = 0.022 [0.011, 0.038] in 73 sessions; Write 28/4479 (lens 4478); Read 7/55258. One session holds 176/644 = 0.27. Inside the 73 plateau sessions, 644/1481 Edits (0.43) fall in the window. PostToolUse progress exists for only 376/644 plateau calls: median 5020 ms after the call, +1 ms after the result. PreToolUse appears on 4/644 plateau Edits and 5588/26323 fast Edits overall, but also on only 5/430 fast Edits inside the plateau sessions. mcp__ide__getDiagnostics appears in 6 sessions, none of them plateau sessions.
checks.problem: The PreToolUse contrast is confounded by session: plateau sessions lack PreToolUse hooks on fast Edits too, so absence of the hook is a session property, not a plateau property. 'Time is inside the tool before PostToolUse' is measured only on the 58% of plateau calls that have a PostToolUse event. The effect is concentrated: one session holds 27% of plateau calls. Nothing found supports the editor/diagnostics guess; it stays UNVERIFIED.

checks.my_numbers: swechat CC shell results starting 'Exit code': 3237; 205 within 1% of the max 10050, in 122 sessions; 10039 x100, 10040 x79. All 205 contain '... [N characters truncated] ...' at char 5019-5025. 215 CC shell results carry that marker: 189 with the 'Exit code' prefix and 26 without, and all 26 have native_error=True. 0 of 57828 successful outputs carry it. Successful max 29766 with no pile; 4 large successes carry '[N lines truncated]'. cc_local: successful max 30000 (3 at max, 12 within 1%, 3 sessions); failure max 10956. aiv_cc: failure max 10040 (5 within 1%); successful shell max 88883. OpenCode shell: 91/1859 within 1% of 51551 (85 sessions); values range 51510-51551; all 91 end with the same harness 'delegate to save context' notice.
checks.problem: The failure cap is measured, not inferred: the truncation marker shows a 5000-char head plus a 5000-char tail. It is keyed to the error flag (native_error), not to the 'Exit code' prefix. The 30,000 cap on successful output is not visible in swechat. It rests on 3 cc_local values in 3 sessions, and aiv_cc's MCP bash success output reaches 88883. The OpenCode cap is a 51510-51551 range marked by a notice, not one number.

Inside one harness (swechat CC), the constant changes with the model. aiv_cc (Opus 4.5, Agent SDK) shows the same 8/10 as swechat CC opus-4-5. The grouping is model generation, which cannot be separated from harness version here. aiv_cc is not 'only 8 and 10' (12 other rows). Direct-API shares of 0.25-0.44 are not a collapse. A Hill α on a small-integer lattice is not meaningful.

checks.my_numbers: 115088 consecutive bash_progress gaps (668 sessions). In [1000, 1004] ms: 91070 = 0.791 [0.754, 0.825]. In [1000, 1010]: 0.878 [0.848, 0.903] (within parent call) — this window matches the claimed 0.877. Below 1000 ms: 7.6%, p1 988 ms. 1005 ms or more: 10.4%. elapsedTimeSeconds steps by exactly 1 in 114467/115576.
checks.problem: The 1 Hz tick is confirmed. '0-4 ms jitter' is wrong: that window holds 79% of gaps. The claimed 0.877 is the [1000, 1010] window, and 7.6% of gaps run early. Jitter is about -12 to +10 ms for 94% of gaps.

checks.my_numbers: Hill α on swechat CC latency: 1.028 at k = 2% (3869). It moves with k: 0.86 at k = 100, 0.96 at k = 439 (√n), 1.20 at k = 1000, 0.75 at k = 5%, 0.58 at k = 10%. p50 82 ms, p99 206644 ms, ratio 2520 (lens 2513). Timeout reached: 535/14170 = 0.038 [0.031, 0.045]. Top 1% of shell calls (≥ 245 s, n = 611): 56 end within 5 s after the applicable timeout (explicit, or the 120 s default); 435 run at least 5 s past it, of which 333 had no explicit timeout and only 4 ran in the background. 611 calls with no timeout and no background flag lasted 125 s or more.
checks.problem: The CI covers sampling only, not the choice of k, and α ranges 0.58-1.36 across reasonable k. Infinite variance (α < 2) is robust. New measurement: 71% of the extreme shell tail runs past its own timeout, so call→result latency there is not execution time. Approval waits are one possible cause, UNVERIFIED. The 120 s default comes from harness knowledge, not from the data.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Block streaming clock as a content-length witness
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For a tool_use block that follows a block of the same API response, the timestamp gap should match args length divided by the session's own streaming rate. Measured honest-baseline rho: 0.815 / 0.919 / 0.815 pooled and 0.579 / 0.863 / 0.709 within tool, at 175 / 197 / 102 chars/s (swechat CC / cc_local / aiv_cc). A rewritten argument of different length would break the rate.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: The rate differs by model and harness (102 vs 175 chars/s). Only 0.31-0.40 of CC calls have a same-response predecessor (0.96 in aiv_cc). Within-tool rho is lower (0.58 in swechat). Stalls and retries inflate gaps. aiv_cu (one stamp per turn), OpenCode and Codex lack the block structure.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Possibly not described for agent-log verification. aiv_accounting reported the block-level version for aiv_cc, and I did not search the literature.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Turnaround vs generated volume (one-sided latency bound)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: gap_input_ms should be at least the time implied by logged output tokens, thinking chars and context. Within-tool rho: 0.356 (swechat, resp_out), 0.551 (aiv_cc, resp_think), 0.401 (aiv_cu, resp_out). Gemini server timing vs reasoning chars: 0.517.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Placeholder usage_out (F2: 0.865 in aiv_cc, 0.782 on swechat subagent copies). Cross-stream ordering in swechat and parallel-call ordering in OpenCode (F7). Haiku subagents running faster (F6). Human or permission waits that only lengthen gaps. So it works as a one-sided bound, not as an equality.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Latency proportional to tokens is common knowledge. Using it as a log-consistency bound may or may not have been described.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Error-burst statistic (lag-1 error autocorrelation vs permutation null)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Within-session lag-1 correlation of the error flag, compared with within-session permutations. Honest CC-family logs: 0.129-0.197 against a null of about -0.01. aiv_cc 0.052; Codex 0.056; OpenCode 0.044. A log with independently injected or scrubbed errors would sit at the null.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Short sessions bias the statistic negative (Who&When). The effect is small in OpenCode and Codex. native_error coverage depends on the tool (F1), so the error flag must combine native_error with text markers. It is a session-level test that needs many calls.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Error clustering in agent traces is probably known behaviorally. Its use as a fabrication statistic was not checked.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Turnaround-latency coupling
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Within tool, slow model turns predict slow tool execution: 0.18-0.23 in swechat, aiv_cc and cc_local; 5/5 independent replications; stream-aware 0.214-0.234. A log assembled from independently drawn latencies would lack it.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: The mechanism is unknown, so the false-positive structure is unknown. Absent in OpenCode and Codex. A small effect that needs many calls per session.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. The weakest of the four. I have no mechanism and did not check the literature.

True per-response output tokens in aiv_cc and in swechat's nested subagent copies, which carry streaming placeholders (F2).

Model or harness version as a stratifier beyond the haiku/sonnet/opus substring family (F6). Non-monotone relationships (Spearman only).

Whether any pair separates fabricated from honest logs. There is no fabricated ground truth, so everything here is the honest baseline.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Harness timeout-ceiling timing witness
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For each tool family, look at the call->result gap distribution in 2 s bins. Within a scaffold, the honest log shows spikes at fixed ceilings: [120,122) s for shell, [600,602) s for TaskOutput and shell. Flag any logged call whose gap exceeds the ceiling without a timeout marker, and any timeout-style result whose gap is not at the ceiling. Measured spikes: swechat 235 gaps at 120 s vs 56/74 in the neighbouring bins, and 173 at 600 s vs 0/8. cc_local 117 vs 3/3 and 75 vs 2/1.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Human approval waits create long gaps that are not tool runtime (O11, cc_interrupt_reject after 16829.7 s). Per-call timeout overrides and different scaffold timeouts also produce gaps. Gaps cluster in few sessions (swechat 600 s bin: 23 sessions), so rates need session-clustered CIs (not computed). aiv_cu shared_turn stamps carry no gap at all.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: using fixed harness timeout ceilings as a timing witness for agent tool logs may not be described; timing checks in general are standard.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Within-stratum template-deviation score with a permutation-calibrated tail cut
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Compute robust z on about 30-39 IR session features within scaffold/stratum, not pooled. Choose the axis-count cut k where the observed count exceeds the column-permutation null: k>=5-8, for example swechat >=5 182 vs 60.1 and aiv_cu >=8 46 vs 0.5. At k>=3 the count is at or below the null. Report sessions above k as candidates.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Several sources of honest outliers: dominant templates and harness caps (cc_local 92/186 template; aiv_cu 35684/78114 at 41 turns), tiny sessions with degenerate shares (aiv_cu picks 9/10 with <=10 events), and loader unit artifacts (aiv_cc failed-resume rows). The co-movement is partly built in by construction. This cut was not pre-registered and was not applied.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: multi-feature robust anomaly scoring is standard; applying it to agent tool logs with a permutation-calibrated axis count is probably not new as a method.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Provider-listed vs executed call consistency
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For each logged provider response, compare the calls the provider listed with the calls the harness executed. The executed set must be a subset of the listed set, and dropped calls must follow the harness's one-action-per-turn rule. Measured: gemini-pro has 39 sessions extreme on unexecuted_calls; pick 6 has 20 unexecuted calls vs 19 executed.

observations.statement: Harness-enforced read-before-edit: in Claude Code nearly every edit has an earlier Read in the same stream. Missing a same-path read raises the 'not read' refusal rate about 40-fold. OpenCode shows the same order without any refusals.
observations.numbers: CC conditional read precedes edit 0.999 [0.998,0.999] 28768/28802 (1430 s). Same-path strict 0.960 [0.955,0.966] 27665/28808; session_strict 0.962 [0.956,0.968]. Refusal without prior same-path read 0.213 [0.175,0.257] 244/1143, with prior read 0.005 [0.003,0.006] 128/27665. OpenCode read precedes edit 947/947, strict 0.815 [0.709,0.908], 0 refusals.
observations.mechanical_explanation: The Claude Code Edit tool refuses unread files (tool_use_error), so the agent must Read first. This is a harness gate, not model preference.

observations.statement: POSTHOC read-gate motif: a 'not read' refusal is followed by a Read of the same path and then the same edit.

observations.statement: Failure markers leave a local retry signature in coding scaffolds: a near-identical re-issue within 3 calls is much more likely after a failed result than after a successful one. Exact repeats after success are rare.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Transient failures (exit codes, string-not-found) get re-issued with small edits. Successful calls are rarely repeated verbatim in coding work.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Harness-gate grammar check
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Per stream, verify the harness-enforced orderings: Read(path) before Edit(path), with a refusal followed by Read and an identical retry; TaskCreate before TaskUpdate; ToolSearch before deferred tools. Honest conformance: 28768/28802 CC edits have an earlier read when both tools are present; 197/205 refusal-retries pass through a same-path Read.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Same-path strictness (1143/28808 CC edits have no same-path read in the stream, possibly context from resumed or compacted history); version drift (cc_local strict 231/1457 with 0 refusals); scaffolds without the gate (Codex has no read tool, Gemini).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Treating harness-enforced tool preconditions as an integrity grammar for logs may be unexplored, but process-mining conformance checking is close prior art.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Tool-vocabulary version/configuration fingerprint
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Check that the tool set and per-tool usage grammar match the claimed harness version or model: TodoWrite vs Task* mutual exclusion (27/4749, 2/1310); per-model get_pixel_coords-before-click rates (0.00 for Claude vs 0.82-0.92 for Gemini/o3/gpt-5.2); cd-prefix and PowerShell style per scaffold.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Sessions resumed across harness upgrades; agent-specific tool provisioning (model = agent = period confound in aiv_cu); small n for many models.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Behavioural fingerprinting of agents/models from action sequences probably exists in some form.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Outcome-conditioned repetition test
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Compare exact or near-identical re-issue rates after 'ok' vs 'fail' results with a corpus baseline. In CC an exact repeat after ok is 0.008 vs 0.131 after fail, so a repeat following an 'ok' result flags a result whose true outcome may differ (or a flaky tool).
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Polling and GUI corpora where identical repeats are routine (aiv_cc exact-after-ok 0.391, aiv_cu retry-after-ok 0.303); flaky tools; subagent retries (0/77 exact).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Using the agent's own reaction to a result as an implicit witness of that result's outcome may be new.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Unverified-completion prior
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Per mutation stream, check whether any test or build call follows the last mutation (CC 0.363 verify, 0.216 test). Pair this with end-of-session success claims; the claims are not measured in this lens.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Tasks without tests; verification by hooks or CI outside the log; regex misses for test commands.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Likely covered informally by claim-checking work.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Failure-position prior for blame localisation
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Rank candidate mistake steps by proximity to failed executions (21/41 vs 11.429 expected under the uniform null in Who&When AG).
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Half of annotated mistakes are not at failure steps; HC has no failure markers.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Probably overlaps with Who&When baselines.

could_not_measure: Fabrication ground truth: no corpus labels fabricated calls. Who&When labels mistakes only.
aiv_cu failures beyond a stderr regex: there is no native failure flag and no 'reject' class.
Whether the openai-responses tool schema offers a bash restart action, which decides whether 0/137 timeout->restart reflects behaviour or schema.
Why cc_local same-path read-before-edit is low with zero refusals: 12 sessions, and the Claude Code version was not joined.
Disentangling model vs agent vs task vs period in aiv_cu, since each model is roughly one agent with its own memory and tools.
Cursor retry and verification (no results in the format); Who&When HC retry (no failure flags).
Codex, Gemini, Cursor, cc_local subagent rates: fewer than 30 sessions, counts only.
Shell parsing is naive: no subshells, control words become segment words, and aiv_cu parses only 0.965 of shell calls (cause of the rest not investigated).
Linking assistant-text claims to the sequences (for example 'tests pass' vs the last test result) was out of scope for this lens.

checks.problem: The numbers reproduce, but three caveats apply. (1) 0.999 counts any earlier read, not the same file, so a single read at the start of a stream passes every later edit. It is not evidence of the gate; the refusal contrast is. (2) The gate is per agent: a read done in a subagent does not unlock an edit in main (36/44 refused). The gate also leaks in the log: 187 edits with no visible read or write still succeed, and compaction probably resets read state (39/128, mechanism UNVERIFIED). (3) 'OpenCode shows the same order' overclaims. Its same-path strict rate is 0.66-0.82 depending on path matching, against 0.96 for CC. Its edits are mostly apply_patch, and file-creating patches sit in the denominator. It has no gate, so the comparison is not like for like.

observations.statement: Every sampled session with IR events has exactly one narration channel, decided by regime: a STOP summary before 2026-03-24, a CONSOLIDATE nextSessionGoal after. However, 180 sampled STOP summaries are platform placeholders, so substantive STOP coverage is lower.

This is so agents don't see each other summaries' (2026-01) and 'No summary provided'. The STOP summary is a channel broadcast to other agents.

observations.statement: The summary is never produced by the logged STOP call. candidate_mechanisms.name: Matched-narration grounding test (self-report vs own tool log with an other-agent null)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For each checkable entity in the narration (path, filename, command, hex id, printed number, URL, quoted text), test whether it appears in the session's call args or result text. Compare that support rate with the support of a same-time narration from a different agent against the same log. Flag sessions where own support falls to the other-agent baseline. candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: likely close to existing claim-vs-trace consistency checks; the low-specificity finding in multi-agent settings may be the new part.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Plan-to-execution chain check (previous nextSessionGoal = next session's goal; check follow-through)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Use the exact chain (1,470 equal vs 3 differ) to check whether commands, paths and hashes named in the previous narration appear in the next session's log. Goal command support is 0.479, while the narration written after the session supports its own commands at only 0.355 (diff -0.092).

candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: cross-session plan-vs-trace checking may not be described for this data; literature not checked.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Narration provenance gap detector (summary not produced by any logged call)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Test whether the narration text appears in any logged model output, and whether its length fits the logged output tokens. Here: 0/25,939 summaries in the STOP output; chars > 8x outputTokens in 0.801 of rows; length tracks the post-session delay (Spearman 0.416).

observations.statement: api_error retryInMs is a deterministic capped exponential band. Retry-wait violations come only from children that are not the same loop's next attempt.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Cross-field timer identities as per-record checksums
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Recompute each redundant timer from the stamps it duplicates and require equality within a few ms. Pairs: Stop-hook summary = first hook start + max duration; mcp elapsed = completed - started; Agent totalDurationMs = result - first nested; OpenCode id ms = created; Codex wall time = exec duration - ~102 ms. Honest floor: 0 violations at 2 ms in thousands of records (0/6714, 0/1147, 1900/2188 within 2 ms, 208/208, 2357/2357 within [-139,-50] ms).
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Bulk re-stamped history (Claude Code 1.0.x gap-0 169/2327) breaks the stamp side. Clock glitches move both fields together and are absorbed (slack +9 ms on the -2.3 s glitch). Subagent ticks reported under the parent id (8879 events) must be routed separately.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: using harness-internal duplicate timer encodings as tamper checksums for agent tool logs may be uncommon; not checked against literature.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Third-party clock bracketing (model API timing headers)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For each model turn, the provider's server-timing duration must fit inside the logger's inter-row gap, and the row must not precede the provider's HTTP Date. 0/12292 violations; min slack 564 ms (gap) and 78 ms (Date).
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Only providers that return timing headers (Gemini here; none in the Anthropic/OpenAI aiv_cu shapes). First rows of a session have no prior anchor. Very long gaps (max ~72e6 ms) make the bound loose rather than wrong.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: cross-checking agent-log timestamps against provider HTTP/server-timing headers as an external witness may not be described for fabrication detection.

candidate_mechanisms.name: 1 Hz progress-tick chain with per-call phase lock
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Ticks of one Bash call satisfy lag >= 1000*elapsed (0/112677), advance by 1 s (delta 1 in 106390 pairs), and keep a constant sub-second phase (per-call range median 6 ms). The first tick yields a per-call execution-start estimate (pre-exec delay median 73 ms, p95 28 s). Inserted, deleted or shifted results or ticks break the chain.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Machine suspend (tick gaps with wall-clock elapsed jumps; 1 timeout overrun, 377/378 gaps wall-consistent). Subagent Bash ticks under Task/Agent parent ids. Not available in cc_local or aiv_cc (no progress stream).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: progress-heartbeat phase consistency as an integrity signal for agent logs is a guess at novelty.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Harness-constant fingerprints
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Plausibility rules recovered from honest data: retryInMs band 500*2^(a-1)*[1,1.25] capped (533/533); Codex 30 s yield cap (0/1682 after cap); Claude Code 600000 ms Bash timeout clamp (9/9 mismatches); cc_local 900 s exit after last event (66/70); first tick at elapsed 2 or 3; Codex ~102 ms wall/duration offset. A log not emitted by the harness must reproduce all of them.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Constants are version- and launch-mode-specific (only measured in the B samples). Clamps make argument values differ from effective timers, so an argument-vs-observed mismatch is not evidence.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: likely related to generic software fingerprinting; specific use on agent logs not checked.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Embedded-identifier clocks (UUIDv7 / OpenCode ascending ids)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Decode creation ms from ids and require id ms <= the announcing event ts (Codex 0/360, 0/77, 0/56; OpenCode assistant parts 0 violations, session ids within 1 ms). A copied or invented id inconsistent with its event time stands out.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Client-minted user-side ids precede server stamps (267/518, median -6.5 ms, min -13.5 s). Redacted ids are undecodable (3545 of 26792 OpenCode parts not decodable).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: time-ordered ids are well known; using them as a second clock against logged timestamps for agent-log verification is an unverified guess.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Timestamp-degeneracy screen (abstention rule)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Flag sessions with tie runs >=5 identically stamped entries or call->result gaps exactly 0. Timing-based detectors must abstain there (1.0.x gap-0 169/2327 vs 2.1.x 329/133590; 10 runs >=20 events, max 68).
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Fast tools can legitimately share a millisecond in 2.1.x (329 pairs). Transient backward reads produce negative gaps that are not tampering.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: a prerequisite rather than a detector; novelty not claimed.

observations.statement: Anthropic request ids are RFC 9562 UUIDv7 values encoded in base58 after 'req_01'. Every one carries version 7 and variant 2, and V >> 80 is unix ms. Newer message ids have the same layout.
observations.numbers: v7|var2: swechat req 154,815/154,815 (2,418.98 expected by chance); cc_local req 31,085/31,085; cc_local msg 30,680/30,680; aiv_cu msg time-format 8,232/8,240. Biased bits sit exactly at 62, 63 and 75-79.
observations.mechanical_explanation: The vendor mints request and message ids as UUIDv7 and renders them as base58 behind a '01' version prefix. The layout was inferred from the data and is UNVERIFIED against documentation.

observations.statement: The request-id server time agrees with the client event timestamp in swechat Claude Code, and split A reproduces it.
observations.numbers: n=154,765 ids in 1,639 sessions. Violations (offset < -2 s): 10, in 1 session. Agreement 0.99986 [0.99971, 0.99996]. Median offset 3,673 [3,558, 3,802] ms on a 53,890-id session subsample; full p50 3,778. Min -4,094 ms. 12 offsets exceed 10 min. Holdout A: 11,047 ids, min -1,001 ms, 0 violations.
observations.mechanical_explanation: The server mints the id when it receives the request. The client writes the assistant entry after the first block streams, so the event comes later by network latency plus time to first block.

observations.statement: In aiv_cu, every server-minted id family has zero violations and a positive minimum offset against the created_at row insert. Split A agrees.
observations.numbers: Anthropic msg UUIDv7: opus 3,481 ids, min 1,297 ms, median 11,607 [10,754, 12,679]; sonnet 2,660, min 1,186; haiku 1,043, min 1,344; fable 1,048, min 3,518. OpenAI items: 14,038, min 450, median 5,739 [5,514, 5,944]. Gemini responseId (LE seconds in bytes 0-3): pro 9,028, min 309; flash 3,264, min 1,448. 0 violations everywhere; holdout A also 0.
observations.mechanical_explanation: The id is minted at request or response creation. The row is inserted after the action runs, so the offset is model latency plus action time.

observations.statement: Id formats change on dates the data pins down. Anthropic message ids went from random 128-bit to UUIDv7 on 2026-07-06. Tool-use ids took the UUIDv4 shape around 2026-09.
observations.numbers: aiv_cu msg: 0 UUIDv7 in 2025-04 through 2026-06; 2,946 UUIDv7 vs 870 other in 2026-07; 3,314 vs 0 in 2026-08; 1,972 vs 0 in 2026-09. Switch window: first UUIDv7 at 20:23:44 UTC, last random at 20:37:04 UTC; 81 old ids after the first new, 3 new before the last old. toolu uuid4 shape: aiv_cu 59 (2026-08) vs 1,003 (2026-09); cc_local 20,415 uuid4 vs 16,123 other; swechat at chance, 2,947 vs 3,022.25 expected.
observations.mechanical_explanation: The vendor rolled out new id generators. Server-side rollout makes the change near-simultaneous across clients.

observations.statement: The skew bracket holds: one constant client-server skew per stream is enough to place every server id time between the last input event and the first output block.
observations.numbers: swechat: 10 of 3,676 streams inconsistent, session-clustered rate 0.0027 [0.0011, 0.0047]; in consistent streams the skew interval width U-L has p50 2,268.5 ms. cc_local: 1 of 847 streams, despite 125 upper-bound violations. aiv_cu: 0 inconsistent for Anthropic (105/80/27/32 streams) and Gemini (255/92); OpenAI 3 of 463.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Causality: the input must exist before the request, and the request before the response. A skew that stays constant within a stream absorbs clock offset.

observations.statement: Client clocks are skewed behind the server in some cc_local sessions. A naive offset >= 0 rule fails there, but the bracket does not.
observations.numbers: cc_local req: 125 violations, all in 3 sessions; min -7,749 ms; main-stream p1 -4,851 vs subagent p1 +1,088. 3 of 18 sessions have a per-session floor below -2 s. Holdout A: 26 violations, min -16,359 ms. msg UUIDv7: 135 violations in 3 sessions. swechat: 1 of 1,231 sessions has a floor below -2 s, and drift exceeds ±10 s in none.
observations.mechanical_explanation: The local machine clock trails NTP or server time, and the offset is constant within a session.

observations.statement: Resumed or forked swechat sessions hold copies of the same entries with identical content but rewritten timestamps. The request-id clock always identifies the original copy.
observations.numbers: 2,060 shared entry uuids in 5 session pairs. Content identical 2,060/2,060; timestamps equal 1,583; 477 differ, all in 2 pairs (297/345 and 180/212). Those pairs have 298 and 181 distinct differences, so the shift is not constant; nonzero |diff| median 12,859,554 ms. Of 561 shared request ids, all copies agree with the clock in 383; in 178 exactly one copy agrees, and the disagreeing copy is the later one in 178/178. Disagreeing offsets are at least 619,473 ms; agreeing offsets run 2,347-21,734 ms.
observations.mechanical_explanation: A resume or fork path re-stamps copied history with new times. The server-minted id keeps the original request time.

observations.statement: Some ids behind an OpenAI-compatible proxy embed a local wall clock 'msg_YYYYMMDDhhmmss…' that runs a constant -8 h from the event timestamp.
observations.numbers: 466 ids in 5 sessions. Whole-hour component -8 for 466/466. Residual: min 2,564 ms, p50 7,766, max 126,285, 0 violations.
observations.mechanical_explanation: The proxy or provider formats its server local time (consistent with UTC+8) into the id.

observations.statement: Tool-call ids from some compat-chat models embed an exact per-session call ordinal.
observations.numbers: 'tool:N' / 'tool_N': N = ordinal+1 for 1,511/1,511 calls in 42 sessions, and all 1,469 steps are +1. 'call-<uuid>-N': 578/578 calls in 16 sessions, 562/562 steps +1. Gemini 'call_<digits>' is not a counter: 0 steps of +1 in 2,441 pairs, per-session Spearman median 0.039.

observations.statement: Client-minted ids that carry time agree with the same client's event clock to milliseconds.
observations.numbers: OpenCode prt: 8,174 ids, min -14 ms, median 82 [18, 159]. OpenCode ses vs first event: 213 ids, median 5 [4, 5]. Gemini CLI call ids: 1,677, min 0, median 11 [3, 14]. Codex session UUIDv7: 77, min 872, median 4,109. 0 violations everywhere; split A also 0. Order inversions within streams: OpenCode prt 2 of 7,961 pairs, Gemini CLI 0 of 1,657.

observations.statement: Ids quoted in model-visible text resolve to the same object wherever both ends are visible.
observations.numbers: agentId vs nested agent id: 2,159 match, 0 mismatch, 940 with no nested events. Notification tool-use-id vs issuing call: 411 equal, 0 different (451 redacted). Output-file name vs task id: 664/664. Spill-path id pointing to another call: 0 (203 own call id, 217 REDACTED, 288 shell output ids). git log subject vs commit claim (swechat): 2,943 agree, 6 disagree after the claim. observations.statement: A minority of references point to ids never issued in the session.
observations.numbers: swechat TaskOutput 16 never issued vs 560 issued before. Notification task-ids: 93 never vs 994 before. Todo refs: 76 never vs 4,677 before. Codex write_stdin: 88 never issued, 12 after exit, 1,615 live. cc_local notifications: 637 never vs 397 before.

observations.statement: Many ids carry no time. Pre-switch Anthropic msg ids and toolu ids are uniform 128-bit values; Claude Code, AI Village and Gemini CLI uuids are v4. aiv_cc has no decodable clock at all.
observations.numbers: swechat msg random_format: 156,277 ids, 0 biased bits, uuid4 shape 2,360 vs 2,441.8 chance. Chance time-plausible decodes, all more than 1 day off: swechat msg 55 vs 52.78 expected, toolu 70 vs 65.29, aiv_cc msg 12 vs 11.93. Entry uuids 122.0 bits of positional entropy (the v4 maximum).

observations.statement: UUIDs printed inside tool output are not tied to the event that prints them.
observations.numbers: swechat v7 UUIDs in result text: 564 in 43 sessions; 440 more than 10 min older, 28 more than 60 s newer, 4 within 0-1 s.

observations.statement: Call ids are never duplicated within a session, and orphan results are near zero.
observations.numbers: 0 call ids with more than one call event in every corpus. Orphan results in swechat CC: 4/194,371, rate 2.1e-05 [4.9e-06, 4.3e-05]. Cross-session collisions of random families match the birthday expectation of effectively 0; Gemini call_<digits> shows 1 repeat vs 0.61 expected.

observations.statement: Release artifacts mimic findings: a REDACTED placeholder uuid, and redacted spill-file names.
observations.numbers: One OpenCode uuid 'REDACTED' appears in 197 sessions. Before exclusion it produced a spurious re-stamped pair and the only non-identical copy. In spill paths, 217 file names are 'REDACTED' and 288 are 'b'+8 base36 shell output ids rather than tool-use ids.

observations.statement: OpenAI Responses item ids carry a 16-hex segment that is constant within a session and unique across sessions. They switched layout in 2025-09.
observations.numbers: hex50 layout: 472 sessions, exactly 1 prefix each, 0 prefixes shared across sessions. hex48 (time-first) only in 2025-08 (126) and 2025-09 (124); hex50 from 2025-09 (41) on. Codex ws_ ids: 50/50 hex50 with byte 01, min offset 1,334 ms.

observations.statement: Server-side ordering within one response is strict: the message id is minted after the request id.
observations.numbers: cc_local: 31,085 requests map 1:1 to message ids. msg_time - req_time: min 44 ms, median 194 [115, 239] ms, max 7,093, 0 negative of 30,680. swechat: 14 of 155,326 requests carry more than 1 message id; 0 message ids carry more than 1 request.

observations.statement: Ordering request ids across concurrent subagents produces many false inversions. Within a stream, inversions are rare and mostly coincide with timestamp inversions.

observations.mechanical_explanation: When parallel agents' requests are sorted by first-block time, a request with a long time to first block lands after later requests.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Server-id skew bracket (third clock)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Decode the server-minted ids: Anthropic req/msg (UUIDv7 in base58), OpenAI item hex time, Gemini responseId LE seconds. Per stream (session x agent), compute L = max(last input ts - id time) and U = min(first block ts - id time). Flag the stream if L - U > 2 s (3 s for second-resolution ids). Honest baseline: 10/3,676 swechat streams, 1/847 cc_local, 0 in aiv_cu Anthropic/Gemini, 3/463 aiv_cu OpenAI.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Re-stamped resume or fork copies explain 2 of the 10 swechat inconsistent sessions; the other 8 are unexplained. Further sources: client clock steps within a stream, layout misdetection (chance-decoded random ids; mitigated by the 1-day rule and the v7/variant check), and corpora without server ids (aiv_cc, pre-switch msg-only logs). Not cryptographic: anyone who knows the layout can mint consistent ids.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Time-in-identifier forensics (UUIDv1, ULID, Snowflake) is a known general technique. Using LLM vendor request and response ids as an independent server clock to bracket agent tool-log timestamps may not be described; I did not check the literature.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Copy arbitration by embedded server time
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For an id that appears in more than one log (resume, fork, mirror), compute each copy's event-ts minus id-time offset. The copy inside [-2 s, 10 min] is the original. In honest data, 178/178 split cases point to the earlier copy, with offsets of at least 619,473 ms against 2,347-21,734 ms.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Tiny n (2 re-stamped session pairs, split B only). A re-stamp smaller than 10 min would leave both copies plausible. Only works where request ids exist.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED; I am not aware of prior use for agent transcripts.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Id-format epoch (anachronism) check
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Classify each id's structure (random 128-bit, UUIDv4 shape, UUIDv7; OpenAI hex48 or hex50) and compare it with the claimed event date. Flag a post-switch format before the switch date, or a pre-switch format well after it. Switch points in this data: Anthropic msg 2026-07-06 20:23:44-20:37:04 UTC; OpenAI items 2025-09; toolu UUIDv4 shape by 2026-09.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: The rollout overlap window (81 old-format ids after the first new one). Bedrock and Vertex variants with unmeasured rollout dates. Switch dates are estimated from these corpora only. A chance UUIDv4 shape occurs at 1/64 for random ids.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Dating artifacts by format version is common in forensics. I have not seen it applied to LLM API ids.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Ordinal counters in tool-call ids
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For id styles 'tool:N' and 'call-<uuid>-N', check N == the call's 1-based ordinal in the session, with every step +1 (1,511/1,511 and 578/578 in honest data). Any deleted, inserted or reordered call breaks it.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: None observed. Coverage is narrow: compat-chat models only, 58 sessions. Behaviour across context truncation or a resume is unmeasured.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Cross-reference closure of text-borne ids
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Every id quoted in model-visible text must resolve to an earlier issuance of the same object in the session: agentId to the nested agent, notification tool-use-id to the issuing call, output-file name to the task id, spill-path id to its own call, Codex write_stdin session id to a live process, and commit sha to the same subject in git log. Honest mismatch counts are 0 for the first four; commit subjects disagree 6+4 of 3,056.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: References issued in a parent or earlier session (notifications 93 swechat and 637 cc_local; Codex 88 never issued; TaskOutput 16). Release redaction. Issuance text the regexes miss in newer harness versions. amend/rebase for commits. This needs session lineage before it can serve as an alarm.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Referential-integrity checking is standard in general; its application to agent transcripts is likely not new.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Session-scoped id segment as splice detector
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: All OpenAI hex50 item ids in a session share the first 16 hex digits (472/472 sessions, 0 shared across sessions). An item spliced in from another session would carry a different segment.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: None observed. The segment's semantics are unknown, so a provider-side change could alter it. aiv_cu OpenAI only.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Server-internal request/message ordering
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For responses whose request id and message id are both UUIDv7: msg_time - req_time must be >= 0 (observed min 44 ms, 0 negative of 30,680), and the mapping must be 1:1.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Only post-switch message ids. In swechat, 14 requests carry more than 1 message id (retries or streaming restarts), so 1:1 is not universal.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED.

could_not_measure: Vendor documentation or stability of the decoded id layouts (Anthropic UUIDv7-in-base58, OpenAI item hex time, Gemini responseId LE seconds, OpenCode 48-bit time+counter). All were inferred from split B and checked on holdout A only; UNVERIFIED.
Verifying ids against the vendor server (whether a request id exists): no API access in any corpus.
The meaning of Gemini responseId bytes 4-16, of the UUIDv7 rand_a bias (bit 75 almost always 0), and of the OpenAI per-session 16-hex prefix.
The re-stamped copy phenomenon beyond split B: only 5 shared-session pairs, 2 re-stamped; the full swechat population was not loaded.
The cause of 8 of the 10 swechat inconsistent bracket streams and the 3 aiv_cu OpenAI ones (not attributable to copies; not inspected individually).
Why 637 cc_local task notifications reference ids never issued in-session: the newer harness issuance texts were not inventoried.
Rollout dates for Bedrock (msg_bdrk_) and Vertex (_vrtx_) id variants: small n.
